neighbours.label: the direction word after an imperative 'come' (come down, come over here, come sit)
fire: She waved from the porch and shouted, "Come down here and help me!"
He opened the door and said, "Hey, come over here and look at this."
My aunt patted the sofa and said, "Come sit by me, dear."
"Kids, come in now, dinner is ready," their father called.
The coach yelled, "Johnson, come here a second."
"Come up to the attic, I found something," my brother whispered.
She smiled and told the puppy, "Come here, little one."
"Come on out, the show is starting," the clown said to the shy child.
quiet: She waved from the porch and shouted, "Bring the ladder and help me!"
He opened the door and said, "Hey, take a look at this picture."
My aunt patted the sofa and said, "Sit by me, dear."
"Kids, wash your hands now, dinner is ready," their father called.
The coach yelled, "Johnson, wait a second."
"Check the attic, I found something," my brother whispered.
She smiled and told the puppy, "Good boy, little one."
"Take a seat, the show is starting," the clown said to the shy child.
